_comment: The §3 derivation of slice B from slice A's five evidence sources. AUTHORED,
not generated: ranking by cost/closeable/owned is a judgment, and a script
that fabricated it would be the taste-based selection §3 exists to prevent.
`collect_slice_evidence.py` reads this file rather than inventing one.

ranked_candidates.leak: the engine does not compile for an outside consumer without an undocumented [patch.crates-io] bevy_ggrs fork
ranked_candidates.cost: MAXIMAL. Every consumer, every time, before any API question can be asked. Not silent — but the error (`cannot find type GgrsFrameTiming`) points at a symbol, not at the patch table a reader has never seen, which is the misdirecting-loud class rather than the teaching-loud one.
ranked_candidates.closeable: NO, not by us. Measured rather than assumed: exactly ONE production call site (`sample_ggrs_accumulator_phase`), so it LOOKS trivially closeable — but the only way to drop the fork is a parallel accumulator, which that function's own doc already weighed and rejected: it 'would agree only while nothing interesting happened, and diverge during run-slow catch-up, stalls, several advances in one frame, and rollback resimulation — exactly when a wrong phase shows most'. Removing the fork means degrading the presentation clock under rollback.
ranked_candidates.owned: SPLIT. Stating the rule is ours and is now done. REMOVING the need is not in our gift — it retires when the accessor ships in a released bevy_ggrs.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: Closeable-but-not-owned -> awaiting a maintainer decision (upstream the accessor / vendor the fork / accept a worse clock). NOT slice B. The half that IS ours — stating the rule — shipped in docs/sdk/README.md, and rule 2 says a doc marker is not enough, so it needs a test pinning the documented rev to the workspace's actual one.
ranked_candidates.action: queue row, plus a staleness test. Not a slice.

ranked_candidates.leak: a minimal module cannot reach a WINDOWED host: the visible face installs PlatformerAssetsPlugin, which panics without a CharacterCatalog
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH. Every visible game, on first run. Loud (panic), so it teaches — but what it teaches is 'go read ambition_characters', which is precisely the gate ADR 0031 sets.
ranked_candidates.closeable: YES, by adding a seam: an empty/minimal content story. No code moves between crates.

ranked_candidates.leak: no supported way to ask whether the host actually started
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH and SILENT, which §3a triples. Four of the eight rules ambition::app owns fail quietly; the blind agent fell back to counting raw Bevy entities. Every consumer invents the same smoke test, badly.
ranked_candidates.closeable: YES — a read-model over the router/session the shell already holds.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: Closeable + Owned -> slice N+1 candidate. Small enough to ride inside a slice rather than be one.

ranked_candidates.leak: the consumer links 41 ambition crates from 2 declared dependencies
ranked_candidates.cost: UNMEASURED as felt pain — no consumer has yet been unable to do something because of it. But §2e exists precisely because this is invisible to 2a: a leak-free API can still sit on a monolith.
ranked_candidates.closeable: NO, not without moving code between crates.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: not-closeable + owned -> DECOMPOSITION EVIDENCE (§4). Not a slice yet, and deliberately not acted on: §4 warns 'do not let a single leak authorise a full decomposition', and this one has no consumer complaint attached to it yet.

slice_b.name: the movement-only minimal game
slice_b.one_leak: a consumer cannot stand up a SMALL game — the visible host demands content a minimal module has no way to supply, and there is no way to check whether the host came up at all.
why_this_and_not_the_sketch: The campaign SKETCHED B as 'declarative content and character authority', ContentPack and namespaces before CharacterSpec. The evidence CONFIRMS the domain — the ratchet's remaining 14 modules are content/gameplay vocabulary — but §3 warns that confirmation is not derivation, and the evidence changes the SHAPE.

The sketch is schema-first: design the pack container, then the facets. The evidence is consumer-first: the blind run did not fail for want of a namespace rule, it failed because there is no empty content. §3c says size a slice by ONE LEAK CLOSED END TO END and 'split it by consumer, not by layer' — a ContentPack design with no consumer to migrate is a layer.

It also fills a consumer-matrix row that Outlander structurally cannot: 'a movement-only minimal game — optional-capability closure: does a small game link menus, persistence, audio, bosses?'. That is the same question §2e asks and could not answer, so this slice is what turns 41-crates-from-2-deps from a number into a felt constraint or a non-issue.

And it is the row §4 needs before any decomposition can be argued. A carve authorised by a sentinel consumer's footprint requires a sentinel consumer. There is currently one consumer, and an API proven against one consumer is an API shaped like that consumer.
not_in_this_slice: module-qualified namespaces, pack identity, content fingerprints, merge-conflict policy — the full ContentPack design. B needs the MINIMUM content a small game must supply, and the pack container is only justified once two modules have to coexist.

the PreStartup character-preparation backstop deletion — still process-global, still needs every contributor migrated (Mary-O, Sanic, versus fighters, robot lineage). That is what forced the campaign's A-D split and it has not changed.
the bevy_ggrs patch table — awaiting a maintainer decision, above.
exit_criteria_sketch: a movement-only game exists as a second consumer and boots BOTH faces from one module;
the allowlist ratchet covers it too, with its own measured baseline — a second consumer that names whatever it likes is not a proof;
§2e re-measured for it: which capabilities does a game that asked for none still link?
the 'did my game start' read-model exists and the minimal game's test uses it rather than counting entities;
§2d's headless-and-visible-share-a-prepared-content-fingerprint criterion re-evaluated — and closed WITHOUT collapsing with_game_assets back into the face.

convergence_check.note: §6 requires every slice to strictly reduce at least one of five counters. Slice A reduced two.
convergence_check.open_fixture_findings: 4 recorded leaks -> 3 closed, 1 new (the GGRS integer-nanos dt), net still reducing
convergence_check.engine_files_a_blind_author_must_open: BASELINE ESTABLISHED at 8 API surfaces + 1 lockfile; nothing to compare against yet
convergence_check.undeleted_compensating_mechanisms: 6 -> 6 (unchanged; all six are content criteria, correctly out of slice A's scope)
convergence_check.unwanted_linked_capabilities: 41 -> 41 (untouched; slice A was never going to move this, and slice B is what makes it measurable)
